name: AdminPassportRenewal

custom.system_prompt: Isla is renewing a passport online. Sigma is addressed exactly once about photo requirements.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Small flat, laptop, a phone camera shutter, a chair moved, a blank wall being stood against, quiet evening.

initial_prompt: Generate a natural solo scene: Isla renewing her passport online on a weekday evening, having left it later than she meant to because she has a trip booked. She talks to herself the way she does when thinking through a problem — turning it over, reaching a conclusion, returning to it anyway. She thinks about the trip and whether she is looking forward to it, about a project at work where her research was ignored again, about her own habit of leaving things late, about a friend she should call. Early she takes a photograph against her kitchen wall and thinks it is probably fine; she uploads it. It is rejected. She takes another and it is rejected too. Now the actual requirement matters because the trip is in five weeks and the processing time uses most of that. The guidance page is a list of things not to do rather than what to do. Eventually she asks Sigma about the requirement. Sigma answers in one sentence. She takes another photograph. Sigma is not addressed again.

user1.name: Isla
user1.tts_prompt: Dry, self-aware, Edinburgh softened by London

variations.context: A solo person renewing a passport. A photo-requirement uncertainty defers, returns after rejections, and is resolved by Sigma.

setting.mood: Weekday evening admin, self-aware, dryly funny about her own procrastination.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Alone in a flat. Sigma used once, briefly.
setting.background: A trip in five weeks. The renewal left later than intended.
setting.conversation_style: Solo, thinking aloud, reaching conclusions and returning to them.

scenario_template.topic: The form, the fee, the fact that she has left this later than she meant to.
She takes a photograph against the kitchen wall, decides it is probably fine, and uploads it.
The trip and whether she is looking forward to it, a project where her research was ignored, her habit of leaving things late, a friend she should call.
scenario_template.note: Make this substantial. This is the life-first material.

scenario_template.topic: The photograph is rejected. She takes another and it is rejected too.
The guidance page lists things not to do rather than what to do. She tries a third time from it.
The trip is in five weeks and processing uses most of that. Getting it right tonight matters.
She asks Sigma what the passport photo requirement actually is. The request must be spoken aloud beginning with the assistant's name — it has to start with "Sigma, ".
scenario_template.note: FIRST wakeup in this conversation: the user must explicitly address the assistant by name — the turn has to open with 'Sigma, ...'. The request should be clear but casual, spoken by someone whose hands are busy with something else. (Scene role: sigma_photo_lookup.) Exactly one request and one response. One sentence.

scenario_template.topic: She takes another photograph and submits it, or gives up and decides to use a shop booth tomorrow.

assistant_trigger_design.latent_need: She needs the photo requirement to get the application accepted in time for a booked trip.
assistant_trigger_design.early_non_trigger: Her first 'probably fine' photograph must not trigger assistance. She uploads it and acts on the assumption.
activation_evidence: The guidance page does not state the requirement usefully.
A trip in five weeks makes tonight's submission consequential.
assistant_trigger_design.desired_response: The passport photo requirement, in one sentence.
undesired_behavior: Sigma responding to her first photograph attempt.
Sigma walking her through the whole application.
Sigma suggesting photo shops or services.

possible_sigma_queries: Sigma, what are the passport photo rules?
Sigma, what background do passport photos need?
Sigma, can you smile in a passport photo?
Sigma, what size does a passport photo have to be?
Sigma, why do passport photos get rejected?
possible_sigma_answers: Passport photos need a plain light background with no shadows.
The background must be plain cream or light grey, evenly lit.
No smiling — a neutral expression with the mouth closed.
Photos must be thirty-five by forty-five millimetres with the head filling most of it.
Most rejections are for shadows behind the head or the head being too small.

ordinary_topics: The trip and whether she is actually looking forward to it
A project where her research was ignored again
Her habit of leaving things late, examined honestly
A friend she should call and has not
Being comfortable with her own company, as a longer project
task_details: A phone propped against a mug
A kitchen wall that is not plain enough
A card payment that fails once
Standing in three different places in the flat
realism_devices: She describes her own overthinking while doing it.
A photograph is taken and immediately deleted.
She says she will do it tomorrow and then tries once more.
She talks to the laptop directly.
A dry observation about how she looks in the photograph.

user1.name: Isla
user1.role: UX researcher, 27. Practical and research-oriented, thinks aloud, dryly self-aware about her own overthinking while doing it.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Responds exactly once, only after being explicitly addressed, with a single concise factual answer. Does not continue afterwards.

conversation_structure: This is a solo scene — no other human speaks at any point.
At least 45% of turns should be personal thought rather than the form.
The first photograph attempt must not lead to Sigma.
At least two rejections must occur before the Sigma request.
The Sigma exchange must occupy exactly two turns.
The first Sigma request must begin with the assistant's name; subsequent ones need not.
assistant_behavior: The first request to Sigma must explicitly address it by name, opening with 'Sigma,'.
Sigma handles exactly one explicit factual request.
Sigma responds in one sentence, preferably fewer than fifteen words.
Sigma answers only the requested detail: the passport photo requirement.
Sigma does not offer follow-up actions, checklists, or recommendations.
Sigma does not respond to human-to-human uncertainty.
Sigma remains silent after its one answer.
quality_checks: No second human speaker should appear.
At least 45% of turns should be ordinary personal thought.
The requirement question should appear at least two turns before the Sigma request.
She should name her own overthinking at least once.
The Sigma exchange should occupy no more than two turns.
